security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged Markdown inline code spans as Ruby shell backtick execution. Review of SKILL.md found documentation paths, model names, collection names, and one manual run command, but no executable shell backtick code or prompt injection text.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can be mistaken for executable skill behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Label the ingestion command as a manual project command and document prerequisites before running it.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks enclose a file path in Markdown documentation. There is no Ruby shell execution syntax or automated command invocation on this line.
The backticks enclose the docs directory name inside a numbered process list. This is descriptive text, not executable shell code.
The backticks enclose an embedding model identifier. The line describes the intended model and does not execute a command.
The backticks enclose the Qdrant collection name. This is configuration documentation and contains no shell execution behavior.

The line documents a manual command for a project script, but SKILL.md does not execute it. The finding is not Ruby shell backtick execution, though the author should clarify manual execution expectations.
The backticks enclose a Python package name used as a Qdrant client reference. This is a dependency label, not a command execution site.
The backticks enclose a collection name for vector storage. No executable command or shell interpolation is present.
The backticks enclose a file path for prompt helper code. The line only documents where prompt construction happens.
The backticks enclose a file path and field names used for personalization. The line describes application logic and does not invoke a shell.
The backticks enclose a class name and a file path in prose. This is documentation for an agent wrapper, not executable backtick code.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose track of how documents become grounded answers in a RAG system. This skill summarizes ingestion, embeddings, Qdrant search, prompt assembly, and agent flow for implementation planning.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the document ingestion flow from scanning docs to storing vector records.
Identifies the embedding model, vector size, similarity metric, and Qdrant collection name.
Explains that retrieved context chunks are inserted into the RAG prompt.
Notes personalization inputs for software and hardware background.
Describes a custom Agent wrapper used for LLM calls and future multi-agent workflows.
limitations: Provides documentation only and does not include runnable pipeline source files.
References project paths that must exist in the user workspace.
Does not define deployment, monitoring, authentication, or data retention controls.
Uses specific model and collection names that may not match every project.

best_practices: Confirm referenced project files exist before relying on the pipeline notes.
Validate model dimensions and vector store settings before indexing production data.
Review generated prompts for privacy, grounding quality, and instruction hierarchy.
anti_patterns: Treating the skill as a complete implementation with production safeguards.
Running referenced project commands without checking dependencies and source files.
Changing embedding models without rebuilding vectors and validating dimensions.
